_source.note: Generated from the pipeline, not edited by hand. Each entity's funFact is its first fun fact marked reviewed: true; no other prose is added. map_click questions are withheld until T-051.

entities.name: Alaska
entities.climateKid: long cold snowy winters inland, milder and rainy along the southern coast
entities.funFact: Alaska is the biggest state, and in summer the sun barely sets in the far north.

entities.name: Alabama
entities.climateKid: hot sticky summers and mild winters, with strong thunderstorms much of the year
entities.funFact: Alabama's Space & Rocket Center displays a real Saturn V moon rocket lying on its side.

entities.name: Arkansas
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers with strong storms, and mild winters that turn icy at times
entities.funFact: Arkansas has a diamond park where visitors can dig all day and keep any diamond they find.

entities.name: Arizona
entities.climateKid: scorching dry summers in the desert, cooler snowy winters up north
entities.funFact: Arizona is home to the Grand Canyon, a mile-deep gorge carved by the Colorado River.

entities.name: California
entities.climateKid: sunny dry summers near the coast, hot deserts and snowy mountains further inland
entities.funFact: California holds the highest and lowest places in the lower 48 states, and they are close together.

entities.name: Colorado
entities.climateKid: dry and cold in the mountains, drier plains to the east
entities.funFact: Colorado has 58 mountains taller than 14,000 feet. Climbers call them fourteeners.

entities.name: Connecticut
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters and warm sticky summers, with all four seasons clearly felt
entities.funFact: Connecticut is home to the oldest continuously published newspaper in the United States.

entities.name: Delaware
entities.climateKid: mild humid summers and cool damp winters, close to the ocean's moderating winds
entities.funFact: Delaware was the first state to ratify the Constitution, so it is nicknamed The First State.

entities.name: Florida
entities.climateKid: hot muggy summers nearly all year, with sudden storms and mild winters
entities.funFact: Florida is a peninsula, which means water wraps around it on three sides.

entities.name: Georgia
entities.climateKid: hot muggy summers and mild winters, with thunderstorms common in the warm months
entities.funFact: Georgia grows more peanuts than any other state in the whole country.

entities.name: Hawaii
entities.climateKid: warm breezy weather all year, with wetter mountains and drier coasts nearby
entities.funFact: Hawaii is made of volcanoes, and it is still growing today.

entities.name: Iowa
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers and freezing cold winters, with strong winds across the open fields
entities.funFact: Iowa grows more corn than any other state, with fields stretching as far as you can see.

entities.name: Idaho
entities.climateKid: warm dry summers and cold snowy winters, especially high in the mountains
entities.landmark: Craters of the Moon National Monument
entities.funFact: Idaho grows more potatoes than any other state, and its license plates say Famous Potatoes.

entities.name: Illinois
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers, cold snowy winters, and strong storms every spring
entities.funFact: Illinois is home to Chicago's Willis Tower, once the tallest building in the whole world.

entities.name: Indiana
entities.climateKid: warm sticky summers, icy cold winters, and plenty of storms each spring
entities.funFact: Indiana hosts the Indianapolis 500, one of the biggest car races in the world.

entities.name: Kansas
entities.climateKid: hot dry summers and cold windy winters, with sudden storms sweeping the plains
entities.funFact: Kansas sits almost exactly in the middle of the country.

entities.name: Kentucky
entities.climateKid: warm humid summers and cool winters, with occasional snow and ice storms
entities.funFact: Kentucky is famous for the Kentucky Derby, a horse race run every year since 1875.

entities.name: Louisiana
entities.climateKid: hot muggy summers most of the year, mild winters, and occasional powerful storms
entities.funFact: The Mississippi River dumps its mud in Louisiana, building new land as it goes.

entities.name: Massachusetts
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters with strong coastal storms, and warm humid summers
entities.funFact: Massachusetts is home to Plymouth Rock, where the Pilgrims are said to have landed in 1620.

entities.name: Maryland
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers and cold winters, milder and breezier close to the water
entities.funFact: Maryland's Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States, full of blue crabs.

entities.name: Maine
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters and cool breezy summers, especially up near the coast
entities.funFact: The sun rises over Maine before anywhere else in the United States.

entities.name: Michigan
entities.climateKid: long cold winters with heavy lake snow, and mild humid summers
entities.funFact: Michigan is shaped like a mitten, and it touches four of the five Great Lakes.

entities.name: Minnesota
entities.climateKid: bitterly cold snowy winters and warm humid summers, with big swings between them
entities.funFact: Minnesota calls itself the land of 10,000 lakes. It actually has closer to 12,000.

entities.name: Missouri
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers and cold winters, with sudden storms and occasional ice
entities.funFact: Missouri is home to the Gateway Arch in Saint Louis, the tallest monument in the country.

entities.name: Mississippi
entities.climateKid: hot muggy summers nearly all year, with mild winters and frequent thunderstorms
entities.funFact: Mississippi is named after the Mississippi River, one of the longest rivers in North America.

entities.name: Montana
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters in the mountains, hot dry summers out on the plains
entities.funFact: Montana is nicknamed Big Sky Country because its skies stretch out over such wide open land.

entities.name: North Carolina
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers, and winters that turn cold and snowy up in the mountains
entities.funFact: North Carolina is where the Wright brothers flew the first airplane, at Kitty Hawk in 1903.

entities.name: North Dakota
entities.climateKid: bitterly cold winters and hot summers, with strong winds across the open plains
entities.funFact: North Dakota's Theodore Roosevelt National Park is home to wild bison roaming the badlands.

entities.name: Nebraska
entities.climateKid: hot windy summers and freezing cold winters, with sudden storms across the open plains
entities.funFact: Nebraska is home to Chimney Rock, a tall spire that guided pioneers along the Oregon Trail.

entities.name: New Hampshire
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters, especially high in the mountains, and warm summers below
entities.funFact: New Hampshire was the first state to write its own constitution, before the country even had one.

entities.name: New Jersey
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers and cold snowy winters, with occasional storms along the shore
entities.funFact: New Jersey is home to the first boardwalk in the country, built in Atlantic City in 1870.

entities.name: New Mexico
entities.climateKid: hot dry summers in the lowlands, cold snowy winters up in the mountains
entities.funFact: New Mexico is home to Carlsbad Caverns, an underground cave system with rooms as big as a stadium.

entities.name: Nevada
entities.climateKid: hot dry summers, cold winters, and very little rain any time of year
entities.funFact: Nevada is the driest state, and rain that falls there never reaches the ocean.

entities.name: New York
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters, heaviest near the lakes and mountains, and warm humid summers
entities.funFact: New York City is the biggest city in the country, but it is not the state capital.

entities.name: Ohio
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters near the lake, and warm humid summers the rest of the year
entities.landmark: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
entities.funFact: Ohio was home to the Wright brothers, who built their first airplane in a bicycle shop.

entities.name: Oklahoma
entities.climateKid: hot windy summers and mild winters, with sudden severe storms in spring
entities.funFact: Oklahoma has more man-made lakes than any other state in the country.

entities.name: Oregon
entities.climateKid: wet mild winters and dry sunny summers near the coast, drier further east
entities.funFact: Oregon is home to Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States.

entities.name: Pennsylvania
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters and warm humid summers, changing a lot from place to place
entities.funFact: Pennsylvania is where the Declaration of Independence was signed, in Philadelphia in 1776.

entities.name: Rhode Island
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters and warm humid summers, with strong storms off the coast
entities.funFact: Rhode Island is the smallest state, yet it has over 400 miles of coastline.

entities.name: South Carolina
entities.climateKid: hot muggy summers, mild winters, and the chance of a strong coastal storm
entities.funFact: South Carolina's official state dance is the shag, first danced on its beaches in the 1940s.

entities.name: South Dakota
entities.climateKid: cold windy winters and hot summers, with sudden storms sweeping the plains
entities.funFact: South Dakota is home to Mount Rushmore, where four presidents' faces are carved into granite.

entities.name: Tennessee
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers and mild winters, with occasional snow in the higher hills
entities.funFact: Tennessee is home to Great Smoky Mountains National Park, the most visited national park in the country.

entities.name: Texas
entities.climateKid: scorching hot summers, humid and stormy in the east, drier and milder out west
entities.funFact: Texas is so wide that El Paso is closer to California than to Houston.

entities.name: Utah
entities.climateKid: dry hot summers in the lowlands, and cold snowy winters up in the mountains
entities.funFact: Utah is home to five national parks, more than almost any other state.

entities.name: Virginia
entities.climateKid: hot humid summers near the coast, colder and snowier out in the mountains
entities.funFact: Virginia is nicknamed the Mother of Presidents because eight American presidents were born there.

entities.name: Vermont
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters, heavy in the mountains, and mild cool summers below
entities.funFact: Vermont produces more maple syrup than any other state in the country.

entities.name: Washington
entities.climateKid: wet mild winters and dry summers near the coast, drier and hotter to the east
entities.funFact: One side of Washington is a rainforest and the other side is nearly a desert.

entities.name: Wisconsin
entities.climateKid: bitterly cold snowy winters and warm humid summers, right in the middle of the country
entities.funFact: Wisconsin produces more cheese than any other state, earning it the nickname America's Dairyland.

entities.name: West Virginia
entities.climateKid: warm humid summers and cold snowy winters, especially high in the hills
entities.funFact: West Virginia broke away from Virginia in 1863 to become its own separate state.

entities.name: Wyoming
entities.climateKid: cold snowy winters high in the mountains, and hot dry summers down in the valleys below
entities.funFact: Wyoming is home to Yellowstone, the first national park ever created anywhere in the world.
